title: Primer
events_chronological: Four engineers - Aaron, Abe, Robert and Phillip - build error-checking devices in Aaron's garage at night, funded by whatever they can sell.
Aaron and Abe cut the other two out and build a box that unexpectedly reduces the weight of anything placed inside it.
A protein grows inside a test object in a way that implies it sat in the field for far longer than the machine ran.
Abe works out that the box loops matter back through time and builds a man-sized version in a rented storage unit.
Abe uses it alone, doubling back six hours to prove it works, and only then tells Aaron what he has done.
Abe walks Aaron through the protocol: switch the box on in the morning, stay sealed in a hotel room all day, ride it back, and never meet your other self.
The two start taking day trips back to play the stock market with the closing prices already known.
Aaron admits he has built a third box, has been going back further than agreed, and has been carrying a recorder.
Aaron lives through a party at the Grangers' house over and over, rehearsing until he can talk down Rachel's ex-boyfriend, who arrives with a shotgun.
Rachel's father Thomas Granger turns up in the present as a double who has come back from days ahead, and is found half-conscious in a car.
Granger's double collapses when Abe and Aaron confront him and lapses into a coma.
Abe reveals a failsafe box, switched on before he ever told Aaron about any of it, that can take him back to before it all started.
Abe uses the failsafe to return to the beginning and stop his earlier self from ever entering the machine.
Aaron, who found and used the failsafe first, is already waiting; he drugs the earlier Abe and takes his place.
Aaron narrates the whole account down the phone to a version of Abe from a plane bound for France.
Abe stays behind to dismantle the machines and keep his other self away from them.
Aaron builds a full-sized box in a warehouse abroad, using workers who cannot read the plans.
syuzhet_notes: The surface of the film is a forward-moving account, but it is narrated retrospectively by one Aaron to one Abe over a telephone, and it never marks which duplicate of either man is on screen. Told-order bullets 8-9 show a stranger's double arriving from days ahead before the audience has any way to place him, and bullets 10-14 then reach back to fill in journeys that had already been happening underneath earlier scenes.
fabula_notes: Primer resists a single chronology by design: several characters exist as multiple copies at once, each with a personal timeline, and the film never confirms which copy is narrating. This ordering follows the account the narration reconstructs, and treats Aaron's repeated attempts at the Granger party as one event rather than the many iterations it actually is. How many times either man used the failsafe is never established.
